dimension.category_description: How AI assistance is spatially composed with artifacts, panels, host tools, chat surfaces, presentation modes, and shared workspaces.
dimension.classification_boundary: Use for visible surface placement and integration, not sensory modality or physical-space registration.

candidates.title: StoryEnsemble: Enabling Dynamic Exploration & Iteration in the Design Process with AI and Forward-Backward Propagation
candidates.why: Four workflow stages—personas, problems, solutions, and scenarios—occupy one interconnected environment, with forward and backward propagation making their shared state and cross-stage consistency mechanism explicit.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: StoryEnsemble ranks over SnapClass because bidirectional propagation demonstrates a substantive shared-state mechanism, rather than relying mainly on the fact that several activities occur around the same artifact.
candidates.pattern_summary: Task stages that were previously carried out in distinct tools, windows, or databases are placed inside one environment where they share state.
candidates.structural_signature: One application shell containing two or more stages of a workflow whose state is shared, such that the output of one stage is directly addressable in another with no export/import step. Only half of this is observable in the artifact — several stage regions plus shared state; the "previously separate" half is a claim about prior tooling, and cannot be read off the interface.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: I retained the consensus top three but reordered SnapClass above Dynamite. SnapClass is structurally more complete because its quotation explicitly identifies the former platform-switching problem and names four consolidated stages; Dynamite clearly names two integrated regions but only implies how analytic state becomes addressable during slide authoring. No score adjustment exceeds 0.3. The main evidentiary weakness is that all selections rest on single quotations: StoryEnsemble does not establish that the stages previously occupied separate tools, while SnapClass and Dynamite do not describe the exact on-screen state-binding operations. SnapClass’s shared state is inferred from the stages operating on the same student work, and Dynamite’s is inferred from real-time integration rather than directly demonstrated.

candidates.over_the_runner_up: SnapClass ranks over Dynamite because it supplies both halves of the pattern claim—previous platform switching and consolidated stages—while Dynamite leaves the prior separation and precise state binding unstated.

candidates.title: GeoVisA11y: An AI-based Geovisualization Question-Answering System for Screen-Reader Users
candidates.why: The persistent interactive map and separate text-or-voice question-answering chat make both live regions explicit. The accessibility use case also demonstrates why a companion channel can materially expand access to a visual artifact without replacing it.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: Chosen over rid 2446 because its evidence identifies the artifact, conversational component, and user questioning behavior—not merely their side-by-side placement—and gives the pattern unusually consequential accessibility stakes.
candidates.pattern_summary: A free-form conversational channel is live at the same time as a non-conversational artifact the user is attending to, and the turns are about that artifact.
candidates.structural_signature: Two concurrently live regions (possibly on two devices): one holds a persistent artifact that is not consumed by the exchange, the other accepts an unbounded number of user-authored natural-language turns scoped to that artifact. Removing the dialogue channel leaves the artifact usable; removing the artifact leaves the dialogue without a referent.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: The final three follow the consensus order; no selection was displaced. Scores were only lightly adjusted to reflect close inspection of structural fit, so no adjustment exceeds 0.3. Readers should distrust any stronger claim about optionality, unlimited multi-turn dialogue, or measured impact: the supplied evidence is limited to figure captions or brief system descriptions and does not directly establish all of those properties. Rid 2446 is the least structurally conclusive pick because its quote calls the right-hand region an audience chat window; its chatbot role and artifact scope depend partly on the paper title rather than the quoted passage alone.

candidates.over_the_runner_up: Chosen over rid 4354 because it applies the same clear companion structure to critical interrogation of consumed media, a more distinctive interaction than soliciting feedback alongside an editor.

candidates.title: PolicyPad: Collaborative Prototyping of LLM Policies
candidates.why: PolicyPad gives collaboration, shared policy authoring, and private model experimentation persistent left–middle–right homes. The layout encodes a consequential shared/private asymmetry, allowing collaborators to coordinate around a common artifact while testing unfinished behavior privately.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: Chosen over DynaVis because its fixed regions encode a more consequential social boundary—shared work versus private experimentation—rather than primarily organizing tools by technical function.
candidates.pattern_summary: The screen is divided into a fixed number of persistent regions, each with an assigned function that does not change during use.
candidates.structural_signature: A stable spatial decomposition of one workspace into n named regions, each bound to a function (input, corpus, codebook, canvas, generated output, controls). Region identity and position persist across the session; content changes inside a region but its role does not. Spatial arrangement may encode something further — process order, or an editability asymmetry between regions.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: The final selection follows the top three in the consensus order; scores were adjusted only slightly to reflect comparative structural fit. The evidence is unusually explicit about named regions and their functions, but it consists only of figure or system descriptions: it does not independently establish user outcomes, and persistence across an entire session is inferred rather than directly observed. Exact placement is also not stated in the quoted evidence for rid 5895.

candidates.over_the_runner_up: Chosen over LLM-box vs. Thinking-box because all four regional functions are explicitly specified and together demonstrate how a fixed workspace can contain changing AI-generated interface elements.

candidates.title: Memoro: Using Large Language Models to Realize a Concise Interface for Real-Time Memory Augmentation
candidates.why: Memoro is the clearest push-versus-pull instance: one memory-assistance capability operates either through explicit voiced queries or queryless predictive assistance, with only the interaction discipline changing.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: Chosen over SceneScout because its explicit-query versus predictive-assistance contrast maps more directly onto the signature’s canonical pull-query versus push-stream mechanism.
candidates.pattern_summary: The same content is made available under two different presentation or interaction disciplines, and a selection determines which is in force.
candidates.structural_signature: One content payload, two renderings with distinct interaction rules (push stream vs. pull query; predetermined navigation vs. free-form questioning; freeform text vs. structured fields; whole-document vs. extracted-terms conditioning), and a mode selector that makes one active. The modes are alternatives at the same point in the flow — either can serve the same user need — and switching between them does not change the underlying content. In several members the two modes are never both available to the same user; there the selector is the experimenter's assignment rather than a control (see the review flag).
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: The final three follow the consensus order; no score was adjusted by more than 0.3. The evidence is concise rather than exhaustive: Memoro’s abstract does not explicitly prove that both modes surface identical memory content or describe the selector; SceneScout’s abstract does not explicitly state switching behavior; and the recommendation-explanation abstract establishes the compared interfaces but gives neither outcome results nor proof that every explanation item was held identical. These limitations reduce confidence in implementation details, but each quote still demonstrates the required pair of mutually alternative interaction disciplines more directly than the excluded candidates. PromptMaker was the closest exclusion.

candidates.title: Selenite: Scaffolding Online Sensemaking with Comprehensive Overviews Elicited from Large Language Models
candidates.why: Selenite leaves the webpage intact while attaching AI-generated support at two identifiable host locations: a global overview beside the page and local, paragraph-level annotations within it. This global/local anchoring makes the insertion architecture unusually explicit, rich, and transferable to other reading and inspection workflows.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: Selenite ranks above IntentPrism because its global overview and paragraph-level annotations define a more precise and differentiated attachment scheme.
candidates.pattern_summary: The generative capability is attached to a host artifact that the system did not author — a third-party application, a web page, a chat client, an established workflow.
candidates.structural_signature: Two separable layers exist: a pre-existing host surface with its own controls and content, and an added layer (plugin, browser extension overlay, injected step, docked component) that renders generated content into or beside the host. The added layer is anchored to identifiable host locations — particular spans of host content, particular stages of the host's flow, particular composition steps — and the anchoring, not the generation, is what the paper specifies. Detaching the layer leaves the host intact.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: I retained the first two consensus choices but replaced consensus rank 3, StoryNode (rid 4124), with LitWeaver (rid 7718). StoryNode cleanly separates FigJam from its plugin, but the supplied evidence does not specify the generated layer's visible placement or host attachment points; LitWeaver supplies the structurally decisive side placement and focus-sensitive anchoring. No selected score was adjusted by more than 0.3. The evidence should still be treated cautiously: each selection rests on a single excerpt; LitWeaver's excerpt establishes the integration structure but does not itself describe the generated output, and the excerpts for Selenite and IntentPrism do not fully document detachment behavior or all interface controls.

It demonstrates both a separable panel-like layer and content-level anchoring, while connecting information gathered across multiple host pages.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: IntentPrism ranks above LitWeaver because it specifies both an added visualization and highlights anchored directly to host content, rather than only a context-aware side widget.

candidates.title: Disclose with Care: AI Scaffolds for Privacy in Chatbot Interviews
candidates.why: The evidence directly identifies both defining regions: scrollable user–chatbot logs and a composition area containing a text box and send affordance.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: Selected above rid 3645 because it explicitly establishes scrollability in addition to the transcript, input, and send control.
candidates.pattern_summary: The interaction surface is a vertically scrolling transcript of alternating turns with a persistent composition area anchored below it.
candidates.structural_signature: Two regions: an append-only scrollable list of turn elements attributed to a speaker, and a fixed input region containing a text field plus a send affordance. New content enters at one end; the viewport auto-follows or can be scrolled back; history persists in the same region it was produced in. This is fully statable without reference to what the turns are about, which is precisely why it recurs across unrelated domains.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: I reversed the two consensus-tied leaders: rid 9215 is first because its evidence explicitly states that the log is scrollable, completing more of the structural signature. Otherwise, the consensus ordering is retained, with no score adjustment larger than 0.3. Readers should distrust any implication that these ordinary panels were the papers’ novel or impactful contributions. The evidence for rid 8454 is also materially weaker than for the first two: scrolling, persistent history, append behavior, and speaker attribution are inferred from “chat interface” rather than directly documented.

candidates.title: Talk to the Hand: an LLM-powered Chatbot with Visual Pointer as Proactive Companion for On-Screen Tasks
candidates.why: The agent is rendered as a second mouse cursor inside the active screen surface, with communication attached directly to that cursor and no dedicated chat-log area. This is an unusually complete match for the pattern: the agent has a persistent, pointer-relative visible form in the user's coordinate space, and its location identifies where assistance is focused.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: Selected over Fairy Cursor because the evidence establishes not only a pointer-following embodiment but also attached communication and the explicit removal of a separate agent container.
candidates.pattern_summary: The system's activity is rendered within the work surface itself — as cursors, marks, live strokes, or attached companions — instead of being confined to a separate conversation panel.
candidates.structural_signature: Agent state is drawn in the same coordinate space as the user's content, anchored to specific locations or to the pointer, and updates while the user is acting rather than only between turns. There is no separate container that owns the agent; removing the artifact view would remove the agent's visible form.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: The final ranking follows the consensus top three; no score was adjusted by more than 0.3. The first two exemplars are intentionally close variants because both provide exceptionally direct evidence for the pattern's attached-companion branch, while the third adds a distinct shared-artifact manifestation. Evidence should still be treated cautiously: none of the supplied quotations demonstrates measured outcome impact; Fairy Cursor's excerpt establishes its following form but not its concrete assistance or state transitions; and CreepyCoCreator relies on a truncated figure caption and a VR-specific implementation. The disagreement around CreepyCoCreator chiefly concerns generalizability, not whether its highlighted, position-specific interventions satisfy the structural signature.

candidates.title: Exploring Fairy Cursor as a Form of AI Agent for In-the-Flow Assistance: Design Opportunities and Challenges
candidates.why: Fairy Cursor turns the assistive agent into a lightweight visual companion that follows the mouse pointer, keeping its presence attached to the user's locus of action. The pointer anchoring is a direct, portable implementation of in-situ presence and makes the agent part of the work surface rather than a detached conversational destination.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: Selected over CreepyCoCreator because its pointer-attached presence is a more literal match for the structural signature and transfers more readily across ordinary on-screen workflows.

candidates.title: CreepyCoCreator? Investigating AI Representation Modes for 3D Object Co-Creation in Virtual Reality
candidates.why: The AI incrementally adds and modifies highlighted elements at selected positions within the shared 3D artifact while the user continues painting. Its actions are spatially anchored, visibly attributable, and interleaved with the user's work, demonstrating the pattern through live artifact manipulation rather than a pointer companion.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: Selected over PointAloud because it shows the AI visibly touching and changing the shared artifact, whereas PointAloud's evidence establishes pointer-adjacent capture feedback but not a comparably clear agent presence or direct artifact intervention.
candidates.pattern_summary: The system's activity is rendered within the work surface itself — as cursors, marks, live strokes, or attached companions — instead of being confined to a separate conversation panel.
candidates.structural_signature: Agent state is drawn in the same coordinate space as the user's content, anchored to specific locations or to the pointer, and updates while the user is acting rather than only between turns. There is no separate container that owns the agent; removing the artifact view would remove the agent's visible form.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: The final ranking follows the consensus top three; no score was adjusted by more than 0.3. The first two exemplars are intentionally close variants because both provide exceptionally direct evidence for the pattern's attached-companion branch, while the third adds a distinct shared-artifact manifestation. Evidence should still be treated cautiously: none of the supplied quotations demonstrates measured outcome impact; Fairy Cursor's excerpt establishes its following form but not its concrete assistance or state transitions; and CreepyCoCreator relies on a truncated figure caption and a VR-specific implementation. The disagreement around CreepyCoCreator chiefly concerns generalizability, not whether its highlighted, position-specific interventions satisfy the structural signature.
